title: Joe Brady Talks Strong Defensive Performance In 23-6 Victory Over The Vikings
headline: James Cook carried the Bills' run-heavy plan in a 23-6 win at Minnesota, and Brady said leaning on the ground game and time of possession is the formula, even with Josh Allen at QB.
summary: Brady called the 23-6 road win over the Vikings not pretty but impressive. The Bills controlled roughly 42 minutes of possession against an elite defense, wearing it down with long second-half drives. He admitted the offense left points on the table, with communication breakdowns, penalties, and trouble finishing in the red zone. The Bills leaned on James Cook and the run game even though the runs were mostly short, trusting that early carries would pay off late, and Brady admitted it is always a struggle to run so much with Josh Allen on the roster. He praised Allen's third-down play and patience in the pocket, while noting Allen would like an interception back on a throw intended for DJ Moore. The offensive line played without two starters on the left side, and Brady cited the depth and said the group wants some plays back. He said the defense looks different since the bye because of its communication, confidence, and selflessness. He singled out Terrel Bernard as a leader playing winning football and said Kaleb Elarms-Orr is being rotated in with Dorian Williams to keep Bernard fresh. Tyler Bass was described as steady and confident, and the Bills now turn to a short week.

signals.claim: Cook will remain the focal point of a run-heavy game plan, including 30+ carry workloads when the game script calls for it.
signals.note: Volume is secure and the Bills are willing to grind, but the yards per carry were low against an elite defense, so efficiency depends on matchup.
signals.quote: we felt like that that was the way to win this football game

signals.claim: The Bills would rather run and avoid a drop-back-heavy approach when the matchup calls for it, which could cap Allen's passing volume.
signals.note: Brady admitted he struggles with running so much with Allen, but the run-first plan can limit his pass attempts in tough matchups.
signals.quote: not make it a drop back fest

signals.note: Moore was the intended target on an Allen interception, which Brady mentioned only in passing and without criticism.

signals.claim: Bernard remains a key every-down defender and a team leader, with Elarms-Orr rotating in to keep him fresh.
signals.note: Good for IDP managers: Bernard is a trusted playmaker, but the rotation could trim his snaps a bit.
signals.quote: Playing really good football and having him out there makes us better.

signals.claim: Elarms-Orr will keep rotating with Dorian Williams to keep the linebackers fresh.
signals.note: A small rotational role that matters mainly for deep IDP leagues.
signals.quote: we want to make sure Caleb's getting in there and rotating with Dorian

signals.claim: Williams will rotate with Elarms-Orr at linebacker.
signals.note: His snaps could be slightly limited by the rotation, which is relevant only to IDP.

signals.claim: Bass is the reliable kicker and Brady has full confidence in him.
signals.note: A stable kicker on an offense that controls the clock and moves the ball is a safe fantasy option.

topics.detail: Playing without two starters on the left side, the line still ran the ball and held possession. Brady praised the depth but said the unit wants some plays back, and the Vikings' protection looks forced one-on-one matchups.
Brady credited better communication, confidence, and unselfishness, saying players are making plays without caring about their own stats.
Brady said the Bills had communication breakdowns, penalties, and missed chances in the red zone and in good field position despite winning time of possession.
The Bills face a short week and move on quickly to the next game.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Loss to Buffalo, Injury Updates & Improving Offensively
headline: Vikings offense is in crisis after the Bills loss: Carson Wentz never found rhythm, KOC says he should have run more, Kyler Murray's Sunday status is uncertain, and a QB trade is possible.
summary: O'Connell put the Monday night loss to Buffalo entirely on himself and said the offense was nowhere near where it needs to be. Carson Wentz never got into a rhythm. Third down was a major problem, with only eight attempts because the offense didn't hold the ball. O'Connell said he should have run the football more and called better plays, including after the early second-half interception intended for T.J. Hockenson. He said the plan was built to get Justin Jefferson going, along with Hockenson or Jordan Addison, but it didn't work. He said the team's practice preparation isn't carrying over into games, even after cutting volume. Asked what happens if Kyler Murray can't play Sunday, he gave no answer and said they'll first see where Murray stands. On a possible quarterback acquisition before the trade deadline, he deferred to the GM, Nolan. Injury notes: Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins hurt an ankle and did not return, Kyle Van Noy was evaluated for a calf and returned, and Wentz was evaluated for an ankle, taped it and returned. Myles Price helped in the return game.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury, did not return to the game; no further update given.
Calf was evaluated and he returned to the game.
Evaluated for an ankle, had it taped and was cleared to return; O'Connell heard of nothing with his hand.
Asked about him being unable to play Sunday; O'Connell said they must first see where he is at before deciding.

signals.note: Wentz struggled all night and never got in rhythm, and Murray's status plus a possible QB trade make his hold on the job uncertain.
signals.quote: we just, you know, never got Carson in a rhythm.

signals.claim: Minnesota will decide its Sunday quarterback plan after learning Murray's status.
signals.note: Murray's availability could determine whether Wentz or Max Brosmer starts at QB against a divisional opponent on a short week.
signals.quote: we've got to, you know, see where Kyler is at first and foremost

signals.claim: The offense will keep trying to get Jefferson touches in space with blockers, and has adjusted coverages to help him.
signals.note: Jefferson was among the intended beneficiaries of the early-down plan, but it did not work, so his volume depends on offensive improvement.
signals.quote: let's get Justin a touch with some blockers out in front

signals.note: Hockenson was a target on the second-half interception and was named as a player the plan wanted to get involved.
signals.quote: we had TJ there on the interception on the first

signals.note: Addison was named among those the early-down plan wanted to get going, but he didn't impact the game.
signals.quote: maybe TJ or Jordan, some potential opportunities to impact the game

signals.note: Brosmer led the two-minute drive at the end and could matter if Murray is out and Wentz struggles.
signals.quote: give Max a chance to move the team in the two minute

signals.note: Price is providing quality returns, but this is of limited fantasy value except in return-yardage formats.
signals.quote: we got some good returns out of Myles Price

topics.detail: O'Connell said he should have run the football more and lived with third downs, and that he needs to call better plays and find better ways to attack the defense.
He said what the offense shows in practice isn't carrying over to the stadium, even after cutting volume. The team was confident in the plan but couldn't make 1 or 2 key plays.
Asked about acquiring a quarterback, he deferred to GM Nolan, saying there has been dialog about many positions and the turnaround is tight after a Monday night game.
A challenged fourth-down sneak was overturned, which was inches from giving Minnesota first and goal at the one. The defense was on the field too much; the kicking game made some plays.

opponent: Divisional opponent on the road Sunday on a short week (not named)

title: Coach John Harbaugh on seeing the fans in a White Out: ‘I know they’re going to be loud and excited’
headline: Harbaugh says J.J. McCarthy looked fine in Tuesday's practice and will make his first home start Thursday night in the White Out; no trade made as the deadline nears.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying the team is excited for Thursday's White Out game and expects a loud crowd. He said J.J. McCarthy moved well and looked fine in practice, and he spoke about McCarthy's first home start as a given. Colton Hood dislocated a finger on a pooch punt early in practice, and it took a while to get it back in place, but Harbaugh said he'll be fine. Cam Skattebo was back out at practice and moving well. On the trade deadline, Harbaugh said no deals had been made yet, that passing on a bad deal beats making one, and that the team would pay a price only for a player it truly loves. He said he would not address the team about the deadline, because the focus is on the game. He framed the Thursday game as a divisional tiebreaker, with the first meeting against Washington having gone one way. He said the coaches planned through the bye for the short week, put most of the game plan in Monday, and practiced Tuesday.

injuries.detail: Dislocated a finger on a pooch punt early in practice; it was hard to reset and he was out for a while, but Harbaugh said he'll be fine.
Back at practice and moving well, per Harbaugh.
Moved around and practiced at full speed; Harbaugh said he looked good.

signals.claim: McCarthy will start at home Thursday night against Washington.
signals.note: He looks healthy and is set to start his first home game, so he's usable as a QB in a short-week divisional game.
signals.quote: He looked good. He looked fine. Yeah. We practiced, we moved. We were going fast.

signals.claim: Skattebo is back practicing and moving well ahead of Thursday's game.
signals.note: Seeing him back on the practice field is a good sign for his availability and RB usage this week.
signals.quote: He was he was moving well.

signals.claim: Hood, who dislocated a finger in practice, will be fine.
signals.note: Minor injury, but worth watching for the short-week turnaround.

topics.detail: No deals had been made as of Tuesday with about an hour left. Harbaugh said he'd rather not make a deal than make a bad one, would only add a player the team loves, and was not personally calling the Colts. Joe (the GM) has been working the phones.
The team has a Thursday night game on a short week. Coaches planned during the bye, put in most of the game plan Monday, and practiced Tuesday. Harbaugh said the team is locked in and focused.
The team is tied with Washington after the first game, so Thursday is the tiebreaker, which Harbaugh called 'for all the marbles'.
Thursday's game is a White Out at home, and Harbaugh expects the fans to be loud and excited.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/10/26
headline: Nick Allegretti returns to starting center vs. the Giants after mostly playing guard; no other personnel changes planned, and Washington is focused on extending drives, red zone efficiency and handling Giants blitzes.
summary: Quinn said Washington is in Giants prep, with Tuesday combining Wednesday and Thursday work before a normal Friday routine and travel. To improve the run game, he wants better third-down conversions to create more drives and more run attempts, plus tailored plans for how the Giants defend. He confirmed Nick (Allegretti) will start at center, after working mostly at guard while others were banged up, and he said a full week of prep makes the switch manageable. He praised the defense's improved tackling and limited explosive plays under the coordinator over the last few weeks. He described the Giants under Harbaugh as a run-committed, time-of-possession team, noted their blitz-heavy approach since losing Brian Burns, and said Washington needs answers to pressure. He flagged Jaxson Dart-style scrambling concerns about the Giants' quarterback, saying his ability to extend plays and throw deep is part of the game plan. On the offensive line, Quinn said two false starts were unacceptable and repeats could lead to personnel changes, but he does not anticipate other lineup moves now. He also said the team added extra red zone reps for the second straight week and did not address the trade deadline with the team.

injuries.detail: Quinn said the last couple of weeks have been banged up for the line; Allegretti, who had been working mostly at guard, will start at center this week.

signals.claim: Allegretti will start at center against the Giants.
signals.note: A settled center with a full week of prep should help line communication, pass protection and the run game for Daniels and the backs.
signals.quote: Yes, yes. Nick will be starting at center.

signals.claim: The offense will work on answering Giants blitzes and improving red zone execution.
signals.note: Heavy pressure is expected, which could affect Daniels' efficiency, but better red zone work may help scoring chances.
signals.quote: you better have some answers that give you good solutions.

topics.detail: Quinn wants more third-down success to extend drives and generate more run volume, with plays tailored to the Giants' weaknesses rather than wholesale changes.
Two false starts were a concern. Repeat issues could prompt personnel changes, but no other lineup moves are expected this week.
Washington has added extra red zone reps for a second week, focusing on quick decisions against man and zone.
Quinn liked the improved tackling and fewer explosive plays over recent weeks, and wants to build on that.
The Giants under Harbaugh are run-committed and play for time of possession, with an aggressive, blitz-heavy defense and a quarterback who extends plays.
Quinn did not address the trade deadline with the team and is focused on game planning.
